m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Foundations Learning Guide's umpire acronym (“So, you want to be an umpire…”), what does the letter M stand for?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Motivated - stay enthusiastic through every game

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Mobile - maintain hustle and be in position

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Managed - accept coaching feedback without question

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Methodical - follow the same routine every game

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Module 1 describes several roles a competent umpire takes on. Which of the following is one of them?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Statistician - tracking pitch counts for both teams

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Coach - advising players on how to play their position

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Communicator - talking and listening effectively to partners, players and coaches

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Sponsor liaison - managing sponsorship arrangements

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the WBSC Umpire Code of Ethics, how far in advance of the scheduled game time must an umpire honour their assignment and report to the venue?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 30 minutes

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: 45 minutes

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: 60 minutes

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: 90 minutes

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The Code of Ethics says umpires must be fair and unbiased in their decisions. What does it specifically say this means?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Giving the benefit of the doubt to the home team

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Deciding without regard to the score

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Consulting both head coaches before close calls

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Favouring the team with fewer challenges remaining

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The Four Essential Elements Theory (FEET) in Module 3 lists four things every umpire must keep in view. Which of the following is one of them?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The dugout

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The on-deck circle

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The base or area of play

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During Team A's half-inning, the head coach visits the mound for a fourth defensive conference in a single 7-inning game to discuss pitching strategy. According to the guide, what is the correct outcome?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher is declared illegal because the team has exceeded the permitted three defensive conferences per game.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Nothing happens - defensive conferences are unlimited as long as they are not injury checks.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The head coach is ejected automatically for exceeding the conference limit.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The conference is simply not charged since it is the fourth of the game.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: After the game, a base umpire who missed a call on a close play at second wants to review it with the crew. Per the guide's approach to crew debriefs, what is the correct way to handle this?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Avoid raising the play at all so as not to embarrass the umpire who missed it.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Discuss the play honestly and respectfully as part of the debrief, focus on learning rather than blaming, and ask permission before questioning another umpire's call.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Confront the umpire about the mistake immediately on the field before leaving.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Report the missed call directly to the UIC without first discussing it with the crew.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During a game, thunder is heard but no lightning has actually been seen. Per the guide's lightning safety protocol, what should the umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue play, since only a lightning sighting - not thunder alone - requires suspension.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait and monitor for another few minutes before deciding.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately call 'Time', suspend play, and direct all players off the field.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue play but move all metal equipment away from the field.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A batter is standing well inside the batter's box, crowding the plate, and is struck by a pitch that was actually within the strike zone. Per the guide, what is the correct ruling?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter is awarded first base, since any batter hit by a pitch goes to first base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter is not awarded first base, because a batter cannot be awarded a base when hit by a pitch that was in the strike zone.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire must ask the batter whether they attempted to avoid the pitch before making any ruling.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitch is ruled a balk and all runners advance one base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a force play at second base, the base umpire ends up standing directly above the bag as the throw and runner arrive. Per the guide's positioning principles, what is the problem with this, and where should the umpire have worked from instead?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: There is no problem - directly over the base gives the clearest view of a force play.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: From directly above the base the ball, fielder, runner, and leading edge can appear to line up, making timing hard to judge; the umpire should work just short of the leading edge at a slight angle.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire should have gone out toward the outfield instead of staying on the infield.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire should have used the Inside-Outside Theory instead, since that only applies to fly balls.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ball is hit sharply into the outfield gap. Per the Inside-Outside Theory, where should the base umpire move to keep the Four Essential Elements in front of them?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay outside the diamond, beyond the baselines.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move inside the diamond, between the baselines.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly toward home plate regardless of the ball's location.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay in the holding zone until the ball is fielded.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A base umpire has gone out into the outfield to rule on a fly ball. As the throw comes back in and a play develops at second base - already covered by another umpire - what should the umpire who went out do?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Drift back toward the infield to help cover the play at second base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay out and let all plays complete, since drifting back could result in two umpires calling the same play.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately return to their original starting position regardless of other plays.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal for time to reset the umpires' positions.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A head coach has already received a warning for arguing a checked-swing call, but continues to argue balls and strikes and directs a personal insult at the umpire. According to the guide, what is the appropriate response?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Give a second warning before taking any further action.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Ignore the comments and continue the game to avoid escalation.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Eject the coach, following the ejection procedure - wait until play stops, be decisive, and use the ejection signal.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the game a forfeit immediately.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A coach wants to protest that the umpires misapplied a substitution rule in the previous half-inning, but does not raise it until a pitch has already been thrown in the following half-inning. Per the guide, is this protest valid?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Yes - misapplication of a rule is always a valid protest regardless of timing.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: No - even though misapplying a rule is a valid protest subject, notice was not given before the next pitch as required.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Yes, but only if the coach files it in writing within 48 hours.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No - substitution rule disputes can never be protested under any circumstances.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base and one out, the batter swings and misses at a third strike that the catcher does not catch cleanly. Per the guide, what must the plate umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Say nothing, since the batter is expected to know the pitch was uncaught.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal safe immediately since the ball was not caught.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Clearly verbalise 'Strike three ... Out!' because the batter is automatically out by rule in this situation, and reinforce the call if the batter starts toward first.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the defensive team to appeal before making any ruling.

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the One-Umpire System overview, what are the "Four Essential Elements" the umpire should always try to keep in view?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive players, the offensive players, and the base or the area of play

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the runners, the coaches, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the infield

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the fielders, the foul lines, and the dugouts

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the One-Umpire System, what must the umpire do on every hit ball, before making any call?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain behind the plate until the ball is fielded

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Quickly move out from behind the plate and into the infield for the best view of the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Time" immediately to reset the defense

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly to first base regardless of where the ball is hit

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Conventions section, how is the plate umpire referred to throughout this manual?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Umpire-in-Chief or "UIC"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate or "PU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire or "BU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Home or "HU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Plate Umpire Starting Position guidance, how many warm-up pitches are allowed for each pitcher in the first inning and with each new pitcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Three

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Five

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Seven

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Ten

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On every hit ball, which side does the manual instruct the plate umpire to exit from behind the catcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The right side, unless the batter is left-handed

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever side is closer to where the ball was hit

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The left side, even on a left-handed batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly up the middle, between catcher and batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: There are no runners on base, and the batter hits a routine ground ball to the shortstop. Per the mechanics for "No Runners on Base," where should the plate umpire move to get the best view of the play?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: With purpose, out in front of home plate towards the pitcher's area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Straight up the first base line, following the batter-runner

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind the catcher and make the call from the plate

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner is on third base only, and the batter hits a ground ball to the third baseman. Per the mechanics for "Runner at Third Base," what movement should the plate umpire make?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move out in front of home plate towards the pitcher's area, as with no runners on base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain stationary behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Sprint directly to first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With the bases loaded, the batter hits a fly ball to shallow right field. Consistent with the "Bases Loaded" mechanics (which follow the same pattern as Runner at Third Base), where should the umpire move?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Out in front of home plate toward the pitcher's area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Toward the right field foul line

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire has moved into position for a potential play at first base on a ground ball. What sequence does the manual prescribe for making the call?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Call immediately upon seeing the throw, then confirm with a signal

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop… Wait… Call and Signal

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal first, then verbally call

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move continuously while calling to keep angle on the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A fly ball is hit to the outfield with no runners on base. Before moving toward the base where the play will be made, what must the umpire judge?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Whether the ball is fair or foul only

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Catch or no catch

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whether the fielder is left- or right-handed

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner's lead-off distance

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball has returned to the infield after a play in the outfield, and all play has ceased. What should the plate umpire do, per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue actively pursuing the play in case a runner attempts another advance

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: May call and signal "Time"

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately return to the dugout area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Call an automatic conference with the coaches

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second base, a fly ball is hit to left field that may or may not be caught. Consistent with the One-Umpire System's instruction to give priority in positioning, which runner should most influence the umpire's positioning?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter-runner heading to first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner on second base (the lead runner)

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner on first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever runner is physically closest to the umpire's current position

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ground ball is hit with a runner on first base. The throw to first base for the batter-runner appears to be a routine, uncontested play, but the runner from first may try to advance on the throw. What does the manual instruct the umpire to do?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay fixed on the play at first base until it is fully completed

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Shift towards where the next play may occur, especially since it is a possible tag play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Time" immediately once the throw to first is released

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the outfield to prepare for the next batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ground ball is hit sharply down the third base line with a runner on third base. Besides moving into foul ball territory toward third base, what additional responsibility does the manual assign the umpire in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately signal "Out" before the play concludes

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay close to the line to call fair/foul

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out for running outside the baseline

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Request assistance from the third base coach

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: While moving with purpose to get into position for a developing play, what positioning principle must the umpire observe, according to the One-Umpire System overview?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Always stand exactly halfway between the two bases involved in the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Ensure the chosen position does not put the umpire in the way of a player or a thrown ball

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Always face the pitcher regardless of where the play is developing

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain a fixed distance from the base at all times

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Two-Umpire System manual, which of the following is NOT one of the 'Four Essential Elements' an umpire must keep in unobstructed view?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The defensive players

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The offensive players

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Under the Division Principle in the Two-Umpire System, which umpire is responsible for calls at home plate and third base under normal circumstances?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire arrives first

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Infield/Outfield Principle, where does the Base Umpire move when the ball is hit to the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Further into the outfield, toward the ball

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Into the infield

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To a position on the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What is the rationale behind the Leading Runner Principle in the Two-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The lead runner is always the fastest runner on base and needs closer supervision

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire must always start closest to second base regardless of runners

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire positions with the lead runner because the catcher is expected to attempt a pick-off play on that runner

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire delegates lead-runner coverage to avoid fatigue

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, what is the Base Umpire's starting position per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 4-5 meters (15 feet) behind the base line, in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: 5.5 meters (18 feet) behind first base in foul territory, 150 mm (6 inches) off the line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: 3.5 meters (10-12 feet) behind first base, on the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly behind the pitcher's plate, facing home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, the batter hits a routine ground ball to the shortstop, who throws to first base. Which umpire has responsibility for the call at first base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because it is a force play

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, who makes all calls on the first throw on base plays

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is physically closer to the bag

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because the hit occurred in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the batter hits a ground ball that develops into a potential double play. Per the manual, what should the Base Umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately move to third base to cover R1's advance

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain in the ready position at first base until the throw is complete

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Anticipate the double play, move quickly toward the base where the first play will be made, and call all plays made on the first throw

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Hand off first-base coverage to the Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the batter hits a fly ball to the outfield that is caught. Which umpire is responsible for the tag-up call at first base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither - tag-ups are not judged on caught fly balls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second base, R2 attempts to steal third base on the pitch. Under the exceptions to the Division Principle, which umpire has the call at third base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, per the general Division Principle rule for third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire has the clearer angle in the moment

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire positioned nearest home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on second and third base, the batter hits a deep fly ball to the outfield. According to the manual, which runner does the Base Umpire take into third base on this play?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: R3, the runner originally on third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Batter Runner

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: R2, the runner originally on second base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither - the Plate Umpire takes all runners into third base on outfield hits

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With the bases loaded, the batter hits a ground ball to an infielder. According to the manual's note for this situation, how should a play at any base be treated?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: As a tag play requiring the umpire to move to 3.5 meters

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: As a fair/foul judgment only

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: As requiring a defensive appeal

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: As a force play

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter hits a ball to the outfield and, as the Batter Runner, advances all the way to third base. Under the exceptions to the Division Principle, who takes the call on the Batter Runner at third base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, since third-base calls always belong to the Plate Umpire under the Division Principle

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire started the play closer to third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because the Base Umpire only covers first and second base calls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base only, and before the pitch, where should the Base Umpire be positioned?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 5.5 meters (18 feet) behind first base in foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind and off the second base fielder, shading toward first base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: In the outfield grass behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind and off the shortstop, shading toward the runner on second base, with a view of the pitcher, runner and home plate area

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire is set up for a potential play at first base and it becomes clear the throw will require a tag rather than a force. Per the manual, what adjustment should the Base Umpire make?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at 5.5 meters (18 feet), since that distance applies to all calls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to approximately 3.5 meters (10-12 feet) to see and make the call

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to 4-5 meters (15 feet) behind the baseline

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Retreat further into foul territory for a wider angle

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and third base, a ground ball is hit to the infield. The defense makes the first play (a force at second base), then throws home attempting to get the runner from third. Which umpire is responsible for calling this second, subsequent play at home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, since the Base Umpire calls all plays including follow-up throws

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, who is responsible for succeeding plays at third base or home plate after the first infield play

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is positioned in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires must call it simultaneously

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Three-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Three-Umpire System manual's 'Four Essential Elements', which four things must an umpire maintain an unobstructed view of to keep the play in front of them?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive players, the offensive players, and the base or area of play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the pitcher, the catcher, and the base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the runner, the coach, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the fielder, the dugout, and the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Division Principle in the Three-Umpire System's 'Two Basic Coverage Principles', when a Base Umpire goes out on a fly ball, which umpire takes all calls at home plate and third base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is closest to third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does 'clearing the catcher' mean for the Plate Umpire, as described in the Three-Umpire System manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Sprinting to the backstop to check for interference

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Taking a small step to the Plate Umpire's left to move out from behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Signalling the catcher to stand up before every pitch

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Moving directly behind the catcher for the best angle

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Base Umpire Ready Position described in this manual, when should the umpire adopt the 'ready' position by unlocking the knees slightly and resting weight on the balls of the feet?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: As soon as the pitcher assumes the set position

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: As the pitcher starts the pitch

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Only after the ball is put in play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: During the pre-game meeting

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Infield/Outfield Principle in the Three-Umpire System, what should a base umpire who is NOT going out on a fly ball do once the ball is in the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain in the ready position at their original base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move out beyond the base line to back up the play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball toward the outfield fence

Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Three-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, a ground ball is hit to the infield resulting in a possible force play at first base. If the batter-runner is called safe at first and continues toward second base, which umpire has rotated into position to make that call, per the Three-Umpire System manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, rotating to second base in line with the plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, staying at first base to also cover second

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire, trailing the runner to second base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 remains at third base and does not rotate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, U1 goes out on a fly ball to the outfield. If the ball is not caught, which umpire is responsible for taking the batter-runner into second base and around to third base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 returns from the outfield to take the runner

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Coverage is shared equally between the Plate Umpire and U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, a ground ball is hit to the infield presenting a potential double play. What does U3 do in anticipation of the throw to second base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Steps forward towards second base to get an angle on the throw

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves to third base to cover a possible advance

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remains in the original ready position off the third base line

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Goes out toward the outfield to back up the throw

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base only, a ground ball is hit to the infield. Which umpire is responsible for calls at both first and second base in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both U1 and U3 share the calls

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on third base only, a ground ball is hit to the infield. If U3 is unable to release R1 at third base (R1 does not proceed home), which umpire may be required to take the batter-runner to second base and make the call?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, after releasing third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire, moving up the first base line

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No umpire - the play is a dead ball

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on third base, U1 goes out on a fly ball. Which umpire moves to the holding zone between home and third base to watch the tag-up of R1, while also preparing for a possible call at home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, before leaving for the outfield

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No umpire watches the tag-up in this situation

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second base, a ground ball is hit to the infield presenting a potential double play. What does U3 do in anticipation of the lead runner (R1) progressing from second base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves into fair territory about one step in anticipation of a play on R1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotates all the way to third base immediately

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stays in foul territory behind third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Goes out to the outfield to back up a potential overthrow

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on second and third base, a ground ball is hit to the infield. If R1 (the runner on third) advances toward home, what does U3 do, per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remains at third base regardless of R1's advance

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves into fair territory about one step in anticipation of a play on R2 progressing from second base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately rotates to first base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follows R1 toward home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the ball is hit through the infield to the outfield and no umpire goes out. As R1 progresses toward second base, where does the Plate Umpire rotate to in preparation for a possible call?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: First base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire remains at home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Second base, alongside U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base, the ball is hit through the infield toward right field. Per the manual's note, if there is a possibility of a play at third base on the throw-back, what should U3 do?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move back out beyond the base line in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain on the foul line even with the base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Release to cover home plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.q

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire's position, the runner's speed, the crowd noise, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive player, the offensive player(s), and the base or area of play

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The starting position, the calling position, the focal point, and the leading edge

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In Appendix 4's Key Concepts and Glossary, how is 'Parallax Error' defined?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: A rule violation that occurs when a pitcher's stepping foot lands outside the pitching lane

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: A visual distortion that occurs when the umpire views a play from a poor angle that prevents clear separation and timing of the elements of the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The delay between an umpire seeing a play and signalling a decision

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: A mechanical error caused by starting too far from the base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Where is the Point of Plate (POP) Position generally located?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly on the foul line, level with first base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Inside the diamond, halfway between home plate and the pitcher's plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Approximately 3-4 metres (10-12 feet) directly behind home plate, aligned with the centre axis of the plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: At the Second Base Diagonal Angle, 3-4 metres behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What disciplined sequence does Appendix 4 identify as the technique umpires use to avoid anticipation and cognitive bias before making and communicating a decision?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: See - Move - React - Call

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop - See - Decide - Signal

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch - Wait - Confirm - Announce

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Position - Track - Judge - Signal

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.q

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 replaces Appendix 5 for umpires below elite level

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 provides the why; Appendix 5 will provide the how

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 and Appendix 5 cover identical content in different formats

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o3

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During a bang-bang tag play at third base, the umpire clearly sees the fielder's glove make contact with the runner's leg but does not clearly track whether the runner's hand had already reached the base. The umpire calls the runner out based on the glove contact alone. Which principle from Appendix 4 best explains the risk in this decision-making process?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Anticipatory signalling, because the umpire prepared the signal before the play began

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Affirmation bias, because fixating on the tag action can cause the brain to prematurely confirm an out and override the actual relationship between the ball, runner, and base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax error, because the umpire was positioned too far from the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: A breach of primary responsibilities, because the umpire failed to rotate to the correct base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A sharp line drive travels near the third-base bag. The Plate Umpire, positioned behind the catcher, is the only umpire with a view of the play. Based on Appendix 4's explanation of parallax error, why is this positioning a concern, and what does correct mechanics require?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It is not a concern, because the Plate Umpire's slot position is aligned with every part of the field

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax may make the ball appear fair or foul incorrectly from behind the plate; mechanics require an umpire to be on the foul line to accurately judge the call

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It is only a concern for home run judgments, not for line drives near a base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire should call the play from memory of the pitch location rather than the batted ball

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner attempting to avoid a swipe tag at second base slides to the back corner of the bag, away from the umpire's position on the Second Base Diagonal Angle. What does Appendix 4 direct the umpire to do in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain fixed on the Second Base Diagonal Angle regardless of how the play develops, since it is the designated starting reference

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Adjust position along the diagonal or move off it as needed, since the priority is always maintaining an unobstructed view of the key elements

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately move to the Point of Plate position to gain a better angle

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Call time and reposition only after the play has concluded

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a potential tag play, a runner runs directly at the umpire, forcing the umpire to move suddenly to avoid a collision. What does Appendix 4 say this situation indicates?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner committed interference and should be called out automatically

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire was in the wrong position or did not wait for the play to develop properly

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire correctly anticipated the play and should hold their ground next time

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: This is a normal and unavoidable part of elite mechanics requiring no adjustment

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During a game, the umpire positioned near second base has a clear, obvious view that the pitcher's stepping foot landed completely outside the pitching lane, while the Plate Umpire's angle does not allow a clear view of the violation. According to Appendix 4, what should the umpire near second base do?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Say nothing, because only the Plate Umpire has authority to call an illegal pitch

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait until the next inning to raise the issue with the Plate Umpire privately

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: If certain, call the illegal pitch, since WBSC mechanics permit the umpire near second base to manage the stepping foot when it is completely outside the pitching lane

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal the Plate Umpire discreetly but never call the violation directly

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire begins forming their 'out' signal mentally while the fielder is still completing the tag attempt, before the play has fully concluded. According to Appendix 4, what is the likely consequence of this habit?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It has no effect on accuracy, since experienced umpires can multitask effectively

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: It disrupts timing and encourages early calling, because the brain shifts focus away from processing the final elements of the action

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It improves reaction time and is a recommended technique for bang-bang plays

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It only affects balls and strikes calls, not tag plays

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a Four-Umpire system, a fly ball is hit into the gap where both U1 and U2's coverage areas overlap, with U1 also converging on the ball. Which umpire should go out first, per Appendix 4?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 should go out first because U2 has the more central starting position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires should go out simultaneously to double-cover the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 should have the first opportunity to go out, since U2 should allow U1 or U3 the first opportunity and only go out if neither does

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither umpire should go out; the Plate Umpire must cover all converging fly balls

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire's initial angle on a developing tag play is poor, but the umpire moves purposefully to a better angle as the throw arrives. Which technique described in Appendix 4 does this reflect, and what is its purpose?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Active feet, used solely to maintain balance while standing still

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The mental snapshot technique, in which the umpire takes a mental photograph from the initial angle, then a second from the improved angle, combining them into a clearer 3D picture of the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax correction, which eliminates the need to change position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The leading edge principle, which requires the umpire to remain at 90 degrees to the runner's path at all times

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A Base Umpire in a 3- or 4-umpire system must decide whether to go out on a fly ball. One available position is closer to the play but offers a compromised sightline; another is farther away but offers a clean, unobstructed angle. Which choice reflects Appendix 4's stated principle for outfield coverage decisions?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The closer position, because proximity always produces the most accurate judgment

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The farther position with the clean angle, because in all cases angles take priority over distance

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither position; the umpire should request a video review

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The closer position, because distance takes priority over angle in outfield coverage

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A developing umpire treats their textbook starting position at second base as the position from which every call must be made, even as a throw and tag pull the play toward the leading edge. Which key principle from Appendix 4 does this approach fail to reflect?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Primary Responsibilities, because the umpire must always rotate to another base first

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Dynamic Positioning and Adjustments, because there is no 'X marks the spot' position - starting and observation positions must never be assumed to be the final calling position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Pre-Pitch Preparation and Outfield Coverage, because the umpire failed to anticipate outfielder depth

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax Error, because the umpire was aligned with the wrong plane

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In Appendix 5a's Four Essential Element Theory (FEET), what are the four elements umpires must observe together to make a correct call?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive player, the offensive players, and the base or the area of the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the base umpire

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The strike zone, the runner's lead, the tag, and the fielder's glove

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The starting position, the observation position, the calling position, and the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per Appendix 5a, the Point of Plate (POP) position is located approximately how far behind home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 1-2 meters (3-6 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: 2-4 meters (6-12 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: 3-5 meters (9-15 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: 6-12 meters (20-40 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 5a, what does 'Backfilling' refer to?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire counter-rotating to cover a position not filled by another umpire who is required to cover a play elsewhere

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire moving to the leading edge of a base to judge a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire clearing the catcher to obtain an unobstructed view of the field

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire returning to their between-innings position after a play concludes

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does Appendix 5a give as the purpose of the Five and Six-Umpire Systems?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To replace the Plate Umpire with two additional outfield umpires

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To allow two dedicated outfield umpires to cover fly-ball responsibilities so the remaining umpires can stay in the infield and cover bases at all times

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To eliminate the need for any rotations between bases

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: To allow all umpires to officiate exclusively from foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5 is divided into four sub-sections (5a-5d). Which sub-section covers the Three-Umpire System mechanics?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5a

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5b

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5c

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5d

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5a: Key Concepts

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.nextLabel

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per Appendix 5a, which four things make up the Four Essential Elements (FEET) that the umpire must see together on every play?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the pitcher, the catcher and the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner, the fielder, the coach and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive player, the offensive players, and the base or the area of the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the fielder, the dugout and the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The elements must be observed together, especially control of the ball and tag attempts, because the correct call depends on seeing how they come together.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 5a, when does parallax error most commonly occur?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: When the umpire becomes straight-lined with the runner, fielder, ball and base or tag point

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: When the umpire is too far from the base to hear the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: When the umpire moves with active feet during the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: When the umpire stands on the leading edge of the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Straight-lining reduces depth perception and can distort the sequence of events. Umpires reduce parallax by adjusting position to keep angle and separation between the elements.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire wants to remove parallax error on a fair/foul call. What does Appendix 5a say they should do?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stand as far back as possible to see the whole field

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Rely on the base umpire to make the call

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the ball to stop before deciding

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Position themselves on the plane of the call, such as on the fair/foul line

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Moving onto the plane that forms the call turns the plane into a line in the umpire's view, so the position of the ball relative to it can be judged directly.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, approximately how far from the base should a base umpire at 1B or 3B start, according to Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners the start is 5.5 m (18 ft) at 1B and 3B, and 4.5 m (15 ft) at 2B. It closes to about 3.5 m (12 ft) with a runner at the umpire's own base.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a play, what distance from the base does Appendix 5a give for a force play and for a tag play?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 m (10 ft) for a force play and 5 m (16 ft) for a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5 m (16 ft) for both

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5 m (16 ft) for a force play and 3 m (10 ft) for a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 m (10 ft) for both

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: On a tag play the umpire must be close enough to adjust left or right and reach the leading edge while keeping every element in front.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: When angle and distance cannot both be perfect, which takes priority according to Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Angle

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Distance

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever is closer to the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither; the umpire should stand still

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Being closer can still help the umpire make controlled movements to a better angle, and parallax error increases with both distance and angle.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Why does Appendix 5a say an umpire must never position directly over a base when making a call?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It is unsafe because of runners sliding

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire's eyes are vertically aligned with the base, so the ball, tag and leading edge collapse into a straight-lined view with no depth perception

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It prevents the umpire from using the verbal call

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It blocks the view of the dugout

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: At elite speeds the difference between a tag on the leading edge and past it may be a few centimetres. A calling position just short of the leading edge keeps the elements visually separated.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Inside/Outside Theory in Appendix 5a, where should base umpires who have not gone out be when the ball is in the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Outside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind home plate

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: On the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When the ball is in the outfield base umpires come inside; when it is in the infield they are outside the diamond. If any umpire goes out, all the others must come inside to cover bases and backfill.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What triggers a backfill situation according to Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: PU communicating that they are staying at HP for the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The base umpire deciding to go out on a fly ball

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: A coach requesting a conference

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball being returned to the pitcher

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: After PU communicates that they are staying at HP, the base umpires adjust: the umpire who has not gone out covers 3B and U1 rotates inside to cover 1B and 2B if possible.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a force play where the runner reaches the base and then the fielder receives the throw, an umpire who rushes the call is most likely to make what error, per Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner safe

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Call interference

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out, because they are still processing the throw being caught

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Fail to see the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: A slight pause on a close play gives the brain time to process all the inputs in the right order, instead of basing the call on the last thing seen.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5b: Three-Umpire System

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentation - Appendix 5c: Four, Five and Six-Umpire Systems

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Three-Umpire System (Appendix 5b), where does U1 stand between innings?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: One third of the way from HP to 3B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Two thirds of the way from HP to 3B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Halfway from HP to 1B, off the fair/foul line

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind the batter's boxes at the point of the plate

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Between innings PU stands one third of the way from HP to 3B, U1 halfway from HP to 1B and U3 two thirds of the way from HP to 3B, all off the lines.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Three-Umpire System, where does U1 start with a runner on 1B only?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 m (12 ft) behind 1B in foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5.5 m (18 ft) behind 1B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 m (12 ft) back, two thirds of the way from 1B to 2B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: On the 3B side of 2B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners or a runner only on 3B the start is about 5.5 m (18 ft) behind 1B; with a runner on 1B it is closer so the umpire can stay in foul territory with a clear view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Why does Appendix 5b place U3 about 3.5 m (12 ft) behind 3B, up to 2 m (6 ft) off the line, when there is a runner on 3B?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To stay clear of the on-deck batter

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To allow the third base coach to move freely

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To be ready to rotate to first base

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: To keep an unobstructed view of the pitcher, runner, batter and home plate and not be affected by the runner leading off on the release of the pitch

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The starting position is chosen so the umpire can watch the whole pitch and the runner's lead without the runner blocking the view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a pickoff (throw back) at 1B, how far may U1 move, per Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: As far as needed, including into the infield grass

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 m (10 ft) from the base in foul territory, but not beyond a 45-degree line through 1B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly to the leading edge of 1B

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: They must stay at the starting position

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If U1 reads that the play will be at the leading edge, they may step inside to fair territory, always keeping the Four Essential Elements in front.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Three-Umpire System, when one base umpire goes out on a fly ball, who takes responsibility for the tag up at 3B?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The base umpire who remains on the infield

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire who went out

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Nobody; the runner is not watched

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The base umpire who remains on the infield takes the tag ups at 1B and 2B, and PU takes the tag up at 3B.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Three-Umpire System, who is responsible for the lead-off call for a runner at 2B?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire nearest the runner

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 is responsible for the lead-off calls for runners at 1B and 2B, and U3 for a runner at 3B.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 is at 1B and U3 is at 3B with no runners on base. A fly ball is hit to the centre fielder (F8, in the normal position) and moves toward right field. Who is responsible for the call?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 and U3 share it equally

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes F8 fly balls moving toward RF and foul; U3 takes F8 fly balls moving toward LF and foul.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 is at 1B, U3 is at 2B and there is a runner on 1B. Who takes a fly ball to the left fielder (F7)?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes fly balls to F7 and foul, U1 takes the right field area and foul, and U3 takes F8 and F7 moving toward CF. U1 taking F9 keeps U1 out of the runner's base path and lets U3 get inside.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: When either U1 or U3 goes out on a fly ball in the Three-Umpire System, what must the remaining base umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move inside the diamond, cover all calls at 1B or 2B, and rotate to 3B ahead of the batter-runner

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay at their base

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Run to home plate

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Go out to the outfield as well

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If the ball is caught and the remaining umpire can take the last runner to 3B and communicate with PU, they should, which keeps PU at home for important plays.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 is at 1B and U3 is at 3B with no runners on base and a ground ball is hit in the infield. What is PU's job, per Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind the plate

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Run to 3B immediately

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail the batter-runner about one third of the way to 1B (further if required), watch for interference, and make the fair/foul call

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Go out toward the outfield

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PU trails the batter-runner for a potential tag, interference by the batter-runner or to assist at 1B, and rotates to 3B if the batter-runner reaches 1B and advances toward 2B.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Four-Umpire System (Appendix 5c), where does U2 stand between innings?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: One third of the way from HP to 1B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind 2B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Two thirds of the way from HP to 1B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Next to PU

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Between innings PU stands one third of the way from HP to 3B, U1 one third of the way from HP to 1B, U2 two thirds of the way from HP to 1B and U3 two thirds of the way from HP to 3B.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Four-Umpire System, approximately how far behind 2B does U2 start when there is a runner on any base?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 m (12 ft)

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 4.5 m (15 ft)

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5.5 m (18 ft)

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 2 m (6 ft)

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Without a runner the Second Base Diagonal Angle starting position is about 4.5 m (15 ft) back; with a runner on any base it is about 3.5 m (12 ft).

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Four-Umpire System, who goes out on a fly ball to centre field?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U2

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 goes out for fly balls to right field and F8 running to right; U3 for left field and F8 running to left. U1 or U3 should be given the first option by U2.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Four-Umpire System, U1 goes out on a fly ball. Who takes the tag up at 1B?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Nobody

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes the tag up at 1B because PU has the Four Essential Elements in front of them at all times. U2 takes 2B and U3 takes 3B.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Four-Umpire System, U2 goes out on a fly ball. Who takes the tag up at 2B?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U2, from the outfield

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 keeps 1B, U3 takes 2B including the tag up, and PU takes the tag up at 3B.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which statement about U1 in the Four-Umpire System is correct, according to the Rotation Memory Map?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 uses 1B foul territory or goes out, and never needs to button hook

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 always button hooks inside

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 stays at 1B for the whole play

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 covers 3B on every fly ball

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 also communicates with PU when coming to HP and pushes PU up to 3B, and clears away from HP when PU indicates a back-fill situation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Four-Umpire System. A ground ball is hit to left field and no base umpire goes out. What should U2 do?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Button hook inside immediately for any call at 2B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay out for an acute angle on the throw from left field for any call at 2B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the POP area to assist PU

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate to 3B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: On a hit to RF or CF U2 button hooks inside for any call at 2B; on a hit to LF the acute angle on the throw is better from outside.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Five and Six-Umpire Systems (Appendix 5d), where do ULF and URF take their preliminary starting position?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind the outfield fence

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: On the foul line level with 2B

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Next to PU behind home plate

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: In front of the outfielder, halfway between the outfielder and the base umpire, up to one metre off the line in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If LF or RF is fielding in close, the outfield umpire should always be in front of the outfielder to accurately judge trapped balls.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: How is fair/foul responsibility divided in the Five and Six-Umpire Systems, per Appendix 5d?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes all fair/foul balls up to the starting position of U1 or U3, and ULF and URF take all other calls

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF and URF take all fair/foul calls

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The nearest base umpire takes every call

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes none

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When tracking a ball near the foul pole, the outfield umpire stays well back on the foul line to have the right depth to judge the flight over the pole or fence.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a fly ball to the outfield in the Five and Six-Umpire Systems, how do the outfield umpires decide who takes the call?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire further from the ball always takes it

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU decides from the plate

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both run into fair territory parallel to the flight of the ball until they have an angle, then the one taking the call indicates with a hand on the chest and/or verbalises

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The call is made by the base umpire

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF and URF are responsible for all calls beyond the base umpire and behind the infielders: fair/foul, catch/no catch and the status of a ball leaving the field of play.
